sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bills for a Chattanooga house?
sections.html:
Two governments bill every house inside Chattanooga city limits: Hamilton County and the City of Chattanooga. The appraisal comes from the Hamilton County Assessor of Property, the county bill is collected by the Hamilton County Trustee, and the city bill is the City Treasurer's job.

The city says plainly that an owner inside Chattanooga pays both. The Trustee also collects for Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy Daisy and Walden, but not for Chattanooga, so a bill from the Trustee will not cover the city share.

  • Hamilton County Trustee: Room 210 of the Hamilton County Courthouse on Georgia Avenue, plus a satellite office at 6125 Preservation Drive, Suite 101. The doors are open weekdays from 8 to 4, and the number is (423) 209-7270.
  • City Treasurer: City Hall, 101 E. 11th Street, Room 100. Phone (423) 643-7262 or email ptax@chattanooga.gov.
  • Hamilton County Assessor of Property: (423) 209-7300, for values, mailing address changes and exemption requests.

sections.h2: What dates control a Chattanooga tax bill?
sections.html:
Bills for the year go out in September, taxes are due from October 1, and payment without interest runs through the last day of February. Interest starts on March 1.

Hamilton County adds 1.5 percent for every month of delay, which it states as 18 percent annually. Chattanooga splits the same amount into 1 percent interest and a half percent penalty. Hamilton County adds that a mailed payment counts as late if the post office does not postmark it in time, while an online payment counts on the day of the transaction.

Each bill is for one calendar year, yet it arrives near the end of that year, so a house sold in spring can still carry the prior year's bill. Hamilton County tells new owners to read their closing statement to learn who is responsible.

sections.h2: How is the tax on a Chattanooga house worked out?
sections.html:
The county Assessor sets an appraised value, a state ratio turns it into an assessed value, and each government then applies its own rate per $100. The city's page gives residential and farm land a 25 percent ratio and commercial and industrial land 40 percent. Reappraisal comes around every four years.

sections.h2: What happens if the tax on a Chattanooga house goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax in Chattanooga becomes a court matter within about a year. The City Treasurer says taxes still unpaid a year after they were due are filed in Hamilton County Chancery Court, and past-due stormwater fees go to a collection agency at the same point.

Once a bill sits in Chancery Court, payment goes to the Clerk and Master at 625 Georgia Avenue, Courthouse Room 300, phone (423) 209-6606, instead of the Treasurer. The city page says a property can be sold for delinquent tax after three years. Hamilton County describes the annual tax sale as held each June, with a one year redemption period afterward.

A stormwater fee rides on the city bill, so a payoff figure should include it. Partial payments post in a set order: stormwater fee interest first, then stormwater fee, then tax interest and penalty, then the tax itself.

sections.h2: How can you pay or look up a Chattanooga tax bill?
sections.html:
Find the parcel through the city's tax search page, or ask the Treasurer for a copy. Not receiving a bill never moves the deadline.

  • Online: card payments carry a 2.55 percent fee with a $2.20 minimum, and e-check carries $2.00. The city keeps none of it.
  • By mail: City Treasurer, P.O. Box 191, Chattanooga, TN 37401-0191, using the original bill with its barcode between October and the end of February.
  • In person: City Hall, Room 100, all year. Full payments are also taken at First Horizon branches in Hamilton County when you bring the original bill.
  • County bill: the Trustee accepts partial payments, and its satellite office at Bonny Oaks handles tax relief appointments.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Chattanooga homeowners?
sections.html:
Owners who are elderly, disabled or disabled veterans can apply for Tax Relief funded by the state, and the city runs a Tax Freeze that locks the bill at its first qualifying amount. A single Tax Relief application reaches both the city and county bills.

The city's 2026 notice sets a $38,470 ceiling on combined 2025 income for the elderly and disabled groups, with age 65 or disability required by December 31, 2026. The maximum reimbursement is $162.12 for those two groups and $844.38 for disabled veterans and their widows or widowers. You must pay the 2026 bill before the application can be processed, and the deadline to apply is April 5, 2027.

United Way will also cover the stormwater fee on the city bill for anyone approved for either program. Applicants who want help with the paperwork can call (423) 643-7274.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Chattanooga property appraisal?
sections.html:
Begin with a call to the Assessor of Property at (423) 209-7300, and move on to the county Board of Equalization if that talk fails. The Tennessee Comptroller explains that skipping the county board generally closes off later appeals.

The county board usually opens its session on June 1. Beyond it sits the State Board, which takes appeals filed by August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice goes out, whichever comes last. Ask the Assessor for this year's filing window.

sections.h2: What is Chattanooga like for a homeowner who needs to sell?
sections.html:
Chattanooga lies on the Tennessee River at the Georgia border, where the ridge-and-valley Appalachians give way to the Cumberland Plateau. It spans roughly 150 square miles. The Census Bureau put the July 2025 population at 194,144, up from 181,099 in the 2020 count.

Ross's Landing became the city of Chattanooga in 1839, and the railroad arrived in 1850. The largest flood in its history came in 1867, before the Tennessee Valley Authority system existed. Today the economy runs on manufacturing and distribution, including the Volkswagen assembly plant that opened in 2011, plus insurance, health care and BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee on Cameron Hill.

Survey figures for 2020 to 2024 count 79,084 households and a $283,200 median home value among owners, with median rent at $1,256. Just 52.4 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so a seller may be dealing with tenants.

sections.h2: How should a seller handle tax due on a Chattanooga house?
sections.html:
Ask the title company for a payoff of every open tax year before closing, and have county, city and stormwater amounts listed separately. Hamilton County states that unpaid taxes continue to accrue against the property, so a balance does not vanish at transfer.

Past-due taxes, interest and any court costs are normally paid from the sale price at closing. If a bill is already with the Clerk and Master, request that office's figure, because it will differ from the Treasurer's. Recording the deed at the Hamilton County Register of Deeds follows the payoff, and the title company usually handles both steps.

faqs.q: When do Chattanooga property taxes become late?
faqs.a: Both bills go late on March 1, five months after the October 1 due date. After that, 1.5 percent is added to the unpaid amount each month.

faqs.q: Do I pay Chattanooga city tax and Hamilton County tax separately?
faqs.a: Yes, they are two bills with two collectors. The city share goes to the City Treasurer and the county share goes to the Hamilton County Trustee, and a payment to one leaves the other open.

faqs.q: Can I get help paying my Chattanooga property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are elderly, disabled or a disabled veteran. Chattanooga takes state Tax Relief applications and also runs a Tax Freeze. Applications for the 2026 year close April 5, 2027, after the bill itself is paid. Call (423) 643-7274 with questions.

faqs.q: What if I never received a Chattanooga tax bill?
faqs.a: The tax and any interest are still owed, since both governments say a missing bill excuses nothing. Look up the parcel on the city's search page or phone the Treasurer at (423) 643-7262.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Chattanooga assessment?
faqs.a: Phone the Assessor of Property at (423) 209-7300. An unresolved dispute goes to the county Board of Equalization, which normally sits from June 1.
